title: Gustar y Verbos Parecidos — Practice
description: Authored A2/B1 practice set for gustar-type verbs: gusta vs gustan, the indirect-object pronoun, the a-mí clarifier, and the family — encantar, doler, molestar, parecer, faltar, quedar.

lessons.summary: Gustar works backwards from English: the thing liked is the SUBJECT and the person is an indirect object — 'Me gusta el café' is literally "coffee pleases me". Two consequences. First, the verb agrees with the THING, not the person: gusta + singular or infinitive ('Me gusta pasear', even with two infinitives: 'Me gusta cocinar y leer'), gustan + plural ('Me gustan los parques'). Second, the person appears as an indirect-object pronoun: me, te, le, nos, os, les. Because le/les is ambiguous, Spanish adds the a-phrase to clarify or emphasise: 'A Teo le encanta el agua', 'A mí me gusta, ¿y a ti?' — note it duplicates the pronoun, never replaces it, and it's 'a mí', never «a yo». The same machinery drives a whole family: encantar (love — no muy/mucho needed, it's already superlative), doler (hurt, o→ue: me duele la cabeza / me duelen los pies), molestar (bother), parecer (seem), faltar (be missing), quedar (suit/fit: te queda bien).

examples.spanish: Me gusta el café con leche.
Me gustan los días de sol.
A Teo le encanta el baño.
Me duelen los pies de tanto caminar.
examples.english: My feet hurt from all the walking.
Does five o'clock seem OK to you?

items.explanation: The subject is los parques (plural), so gustan — the verb agrees with the thing liked.

items.promptEnglish: We like walking in the morning.
items.explanation: An infinitive counts as singular: gusta + pasear.

items.prompt: A Teo ___ encanta el agua de la bañera. (pronombre)
items.explanation: The a-phrase (a Teo) duplicates the pronoun, it never replaces it: a Teo LE encanta.
After a, the pronoun is mí: a mí. «A yo» doesn't exist, and plain yo doesn't work with gustar-verbs.

items.prompt: Me ___ los brazos de cargarlo todo el día. (doler, presente)
items.promptEnglish: My arms hurt from carrying him all day.
items.explanation: Doler works like gustar and agrees with los brazos: duelen (o→ue).
La pancita is singular → duele. The person shows up as le, not as the subject.

items.promptEnglish: Does the noise from the building site bother you?
items.explanation: Molestar takes the gustar pattern: el ruido (singular) molesta, and you appear as te.

items.prompt: ¿Qué te ___ si vamos a la plaza? (parecer, presente)
items.promptEnglish: What do you think about going to the square?
items.explanation: Parecer: the idea is the subject, you are te — ¿qué te parece?

items.prompt: Nos ___ los pañales — hay que comprar más.
items.promptEnglish: We're out of nappies — we need to buy more.
items.explanation: Faltar agrees with what's missing: los pañales → faltan.

items.prompt: A mis padres ___ gusta venir a vernos.
items.promptEnglish: My parents like coming to see us.
items.explanation: Mis padres is plural, so les. (Los is a direct-object pronoun — the wrong family.)

items.prompt: Ese gorrito te ___ muy bien. (quedar, presente)
items.promptEnglish: That little hat really suits you.
items.explanation: Quedar bien/mal works like gustar: el gorrito queda, and the wearer is te.
Encantar is already superlative — «me encanta mucho» over-eggs it. Just me encanta.
